title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 285
paragraphs: There are many ways in use of catching them, of various kinds; I shall describe the one that to me seems the most worthy of being told. A man puts the back of a pig upon a hook as bait, and lets it go into the middle of the river, while he himself on the bank has a young live pig, which he beats; and the crocodile, hearing its cries, makes for the direction of the sound, and when he finds the pig's back he swallows it down. Then they pull; and when he is drawn out to land, the hunter at once plasters up his eyes with mud, and having done so he very easily gets the mastery of him — but if he does not do so, he has much trouble.
